note.question: How can the OEM digitize the spare parts supply chain by leveraging 3D printing via intellectual property (IP) licensing?
note.overview: The model considers an OEM supplying a single part to multiple buyers over an infinite horizon. This paper studies how the OEM can digitize the spare parts supply chain by leveraging 3D printing via intellectual property (IP) licensing. Additive manufacturing, also known as 3D printing, has the potential to shift supply chains from global networks that rely on centralized production with traditional manufacturing technologies to mainly digital networks with distributed, local printing.

source.quote: Problem definition: We consider an OEM supplying a single part to multiple buyers over an infinite horizon.
Particularly well positioned to drive this transition are original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) who design and produce capital goods.
With the license agreement, a buyer can print parts locally through a third-party printing service provider, enjoying a shorter lead time and lower setup cost.
However, most of our results can be generalized to exogenous and sequential stochastic lead times.
Let Di denote buyer i’s lead time demand.
With the IP license, a buyer is able to 3D print spare parts locally from a third-party PSP at a unit printing price p, which is market driven and thus exogenous.
